feeds.title: Feed addresses
feeds.description: One or more RSS, Atom or JSON Feed addresses, separated by commas. A site's home page works too when it advertises its feed.

maxItemsPerFeed.title: Newest items to read from each feed

setupInstructions.title: No sign-in needed
setupInstructions.description: Paste the address of any public RSS, Atom or JSON feed. Gezel checks each feed politely, asking only for what changed, and keeps every item it has seen.
steps: Copy the feed address from the site (often a link labeled RSS, Feed or Subscribe), or paste the site's home page and Gezel will look for the feed it advertises.
Add more feeds separated by commas. Each feed gets its own folder.
Feeds that need a password are not supported. Never put a password in a feed address.

notes: Reads RSS 2.0, RSS 1.0 (RDF), Atom 1.0 and JSON Feed 1.0/1.1, one folder per feed and one file per item, bucketed by month of the item's date (undated items go under undated/). A feed only lists its publisher's newest items, so this is a window: the first sync captures what each feed currently carries (up to maxItemsPerFeed, newest first) and older posts are never backfilled. Items that later drop off a feed stay in the corpus; nothing is deleted. An edited item (same guid) is refreshed in place. Each check is a conditional request (ETag / Last-Modified), so an unchanged feed costs one small request and writes nothing. HTML content is converted to markdown with relative links made absolute; item titles, authors, categories, the permalink and the feed's name are kept as frontmatter. Podcast and media enclosures are recorded as a link with their type and size and are never downloaded. Limits: 5 MB per feed document, 30 seconds per request, at most 5 redirects; a redirect or advertised feed pointing at a non-web address, at an address carrying credentials, or from a public site into a private network is refused. A feed that answers 429 or 503 pauses the whole connector briefly. A broken feed fails only its own folder while the other feeds keep syncing. Feeds that need a sign-in are not supported and credentials in a feed address are refused; a token in the query string of a private podcast address is masked in what records show, but a token inside the address path is visible to gezels reading the corpus. Tip: a YouTube channel can be followed without an API key through https://www.youtube.com/feeds/videos.xml?channel_id=UC… (its newest 15 videos, without view counts).
